summary: A toggle for an on/off setting that takes effect as a form field: it submits a value while on, resets with its form, is disabled by a disabled fieldset and validates required. Operable by keyboard, with a label, a description, an error message and two sizes.

checked.note: On or off. The native-input spelling of the vocabulary's `selected` (registered alias checked -> selected). Initial state from the attribute; after the user toggles it, the property is the source of truth. form.reset() returns it to the initial attribute value.

label.note: The visible text and the accessible name. A missing label logs a console warning (the name cannot come from <label for>, which does not name the host).

description.note: A hint under the label, read with the control.

errorMessage.note: Why the value is not accepted. Shown, and read with the control, only while validation is error.

validation.note: error shows the error look and marks the control invalid for assistive technology. Set by the author; never inferred from required validity.

size.note: Track and thumb size step (registered aliases: default -> medium, sm -> small).

name.note: The name the value is submitted under. Without a name nothing is submitted.

value.note: What the form submits while the switch is on, like a native checkbox. An off switch submits nothing.

required.note: The switch must be on for the form to be valid (native checkbox semantics: valueMissing while off).

disabled.note: Cannot be focused, toggled or submitted. A disabled ancestor fieldset has the same effect without changing this property.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.notes: Row: the control beside the content column.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: The switch itself: the focusable control that holds the track and the thumb.

anatomy.name: track
anatomy.notes: The pill the thumb slides in; its fill shows on or off.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: The knob; sits at the start when off and at the end when on.

anatomy.name: content
anatomy.notes: Column beside the control: label, description and error message.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Shown only while validation is error and an error message is set.

excludedCombinations.reason: A disabled field is not validated, so it never shows the error look.

change.note: The user toggled the switch. Fires after `checked` and the form value are updated, so a listener reads the new value from the property and from FormData. Not fired when the property or attribute is set by code.

hover.trigger: Pointer over the control or its label.
hover.note: No color change; the pointer cursor is the only hover cue. PROPOSAL: revisit if a design review wants a hover fill.

disabled.trigger: disabled is true, or a disabled ancestor fieldset.

accessibility.native: A native checkbox input carries the switch role, checked state, Space toggling and the focus ring; the host adds no ARIA state of its own.
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, on the inner control. A <label for> activates the control but does not name it.

formAssociation.note: Form-associated through the shared mixin. Submits `value` under `name` only while on; form.reset() restores the initial checked state; a disabled fieldset disables it and re-enabling restores it without touching the disabled attribute; required makes an off switch invalid (valueMissing) and reportValidity() focuses the control; a <label for> click toggles it. Standalone control, not a group member: no exclusivity or roving focus.

accessibility.targetSize: The control is at least 24x24 CSS px at both sizes (WCAG 2.5.8); the label is part of the click target.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: A ring of the focus ring width in the ring color, at least 3:1 against the background, shown for keyboard focus only.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: A console warning when the switch has no label.

keyboard.Tab: Moves focus to the switch, or past it.
keyboard.Enter: Does not toggle; submits the owning form (implicit submission), like a native checkbox.

aria: role=switch with the native checked state, on the inner input
aria-describedby points at the description and, while validation is error, the error message
No aria-label or aria-labelledby: the name is the visible label
announcements: Name, role switch and on/off state on focus.
State change on toggle, from the native checked state.
Description and error message read after the name.

useCases.when: A setting is on or off and the change is the choice (notifications, dark mode, airplane mode).
The setting needs context or may be refused.
useCases.use: Add description for the hint, or validation="error" with errorMessage for the refusal.

useCases.when: A settings list is dense, or the switch sits in a toolbar-like row.
The switch must be on before the form can be submitted (accept the terms of a feature).
useCases.use: required, with errorMessage shown through validation="error" after a failed submit.

antiPatterns.why: The APG switch pattern requires an accessible name, and a <label for> does not name the host; the component warns in the console.
antiPatterns.alternative: Always pass label, even when the design shows it elsewhere.

openQuestions.question: Spell the on/off prop `checked` (the native name, registered alias of `selected`) or the canonical `selected`?
openQuestions.recommendation: checked: the host behaves like an input, and consumers read el.checked and :checked.
openQuestions.answer: checked, through the registered alias. The design file still names the axis Selected.

openQuestions.question: Should Enter toggle the switch? The APG makes it optional.
openQuestions.recommendation: No. Space toggles; Enter submits the form like a native checkbox.
openQuestions.answer: Enter does not toggle and submits the owning form.

openQuestions.question: Should the error look appear automatically when required validity fails?
openQuestions.recommendation: No. validation is author-controlled, like the other form controls; native validity still blocks submit and reportValidity() focuses the control.
openQuestions.answer: validation is set by the author only.

openQuestions.question: Does the switch need label placement (label before the control) or on/off text inside the track?
openQuestions.recommendation: Neither: not requested. The label follows the control; add either later with its own contract change.

openQuestions.question: Is a manual screen-reader pass needed before stable?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes: VoiceOver and NVDA announce name, switch role, state and description/error, because axe cannot judge announcements.
openQuestions.answer: Required before the move from beta to stable; listed in plan.md.
